title: Gen Z initiative holds nationwide demonstrations across Germany
seoTitle: Berlin Gen Z initiative nationwide demonstrations

tea.why: Young people are protesting due to rising living costs, poor school conditions, and government budget cuts affecting younger generations.
tea.want: Protesters are demanding better education investment, lower living costs, and opposition to compulsory military service.
tea.changed: Nov 1: Authorities reported dozens of arrests and multiple police injuries following evening disturbances in cities like Berlin and Frankfurt.

summary: Thousands of people participated in nationwide demonstrations across more than thirty cities in Germany, organized by the campaign group "Gen Z regelt." The youth-led movement aimed to draw attention to increasing living expenses, education deterioration, and the potential reintroduction of compulsory military service. Turnout figures varied, with organizers estimating around 120,000 participants nationwide, while initial official counts were significantly lower. In Berlin, thousands gathered near the Brandenburg Gate. Although daytime rallies were largely reported as peaceful, evening tensions erupted in several cities, including Frankfurt, Cologne, and Hamburg, leading to clashes, property damage, police injuries, and numerous arrests. Government officials condemned the violence, while the organizers distanced themselves from the unrest.
response: Federal and state interior ministers condemned the evening violence, announced strict penalties for rioters, and blamed extremist groups and trouble-makers for hijacking the protests. Meanwhile, some political figures called for a national education summit.

injuries.text: 27 police officers slightly injured in Berlin

updates.text: Demonstrations organized by "Gen Z regelt" took place across numerous German cities, drawing thousands of participants.
Authorities reported evening clashes, property damage, and numerous arrests in cities including Berlin, Frankfurt, and Cologne.
